signals: current-sensor (BJB) phase-current ripple waveform at high motor speed; motor speed; PEB torque-cut / fail-safe state
note: Current sensor in junction box misdiagnoses a gap in motor current-ripple frequency at high speed; inverter cuts torque. Remedy: inverter fail-safe software. Description of cause NR. Seeing the ripple gap needs a high-rate current trace before the trip; a snapshot shows only the fault state. RMISC attachment image-only (no text).

signals: none (locates only: front-end noise, suspension failure)
note: Under-torqued steer-axle spring-hanger fasteners found by plant quality control.

signals: none (locates only: pretensioner non-deployment in a crash)
note: Pretensioner clutch pawls and O-ring missing from assembly; found at supplier deployment test and teardown.

signals: LDC (12 V converter) output voltage at charge-cycle start and end; MOSFET / power-stage temperature; coolant and fan state over the charge or drive; ICCU fuse state
note: ICCU low-voltage converter MOSFET fails: two stated causes, overvoltage at start and end of the battery charging cycle (transient) and thermal loading during charging and driving (minutes). Window set by the thermal-loading leg; the rate by the overvoltage transient. Evidence: returned-part inspection and CT scan.

signals: inverter phase/DC current versus broadcast current limit; battery current; contactor state; SOC (regen at high SOC)
note: Inverter firmware mis-estimates broadcast current, overshoots the current limit, battery contactors open. Over-current is an electrical event, so not software-only.

signals: none (locates only: string-open / fuse-blown warning, abnormal module voltage and temperature)
note: Inadequate weld penetration on a busbar (J-bar) inside the battery module separates, arcs and overheats a cell; co-cause: BMS software does not lock out the pack. The remedy detects high-resistance behaviour from voltage and temperature, so a signal could flag a bad joint but not the stated cause (weld penetration). Defective part is inside the traction-battery module, hence out-of-scope flag; BMS software co-cause is in scope.

signals: none (locates only: wheel-nut crack / wheel looseness)
note: Center-lock wheel nut cracks: lack of fusion in Tier-2 hollow aluminium extrusion.

signals: ICCU / LDC output and HV-side voltage transients; power-stage temperature history across charge and drive cycles; 12 V battery voltage
note: ICCU damaged over time by transient high voltage and thermal cycling (two stated causes; document states cumulative damage over time, hence >700 s). Chronology is field-case counts only.

signals: HEV ECU output-limit value versus BMS output-limit demand; HV battery and cell voltage; accelerator pedal position; EV-mode flag; battery temperature
note: HEV ECU output-limit calculation does not follow the battery output-limit demand; rapid pedal after cold EV-mode driving pulls cell voltage below threshold, system ready-off. Freeze frame showed EV mode and cold; mechanism found on chassis dynamometer. Seeing limit vs demand over the pedal tip-in needs seconds. Defective module is the vehicle-level hybrid control ECU, so out-of-scope flagged (judgement).

signals: none (locates only: airbag deployment anomaly in a crash)
note: Passenger airbag score-line possibly missing on three instrument panels; supplier production-tracking error. Identified from production data.

signals: none (locates only: buckle rattle / restraint performance in a crash)
note: Seat-belt buckle bolt not torqued; supplier torque-controller attributed another bolt reading.

signals: isolation-fault DTC and fault-severity class at the trip; HV shutdown state; gear state
note: Vehicle control software misclassifies a loss of isolation as a severe fault and shuts the HV system in motion. The DTC set and the shutdown state at the trip identify it. Isolation loss is an electrical event, so not software-only. Defective module is the vehicle/powertrain controller, so out-of-scope flagged (judgement).

signals: none (locates only: misalignment / steering pull)
note: Wheel-alignment ring installed at the wrong angle at the plant; found by inspection. Description of cause NR but the defect text states the assembly error.

signals: none (locates only: HV shutdown / short at disconnect-switch terminals)
note: Fuse-box / disconnect-switch bracket fatigues under switch mass and vibration and breaks; terminals short to chassis. Mechanical design weakness; the defective part is a bracket.

signals: LDC/ICCU current and output voltage (over-current, end-of-charge overvoltage peak); power-stage and coolant temperature, water-pump state over charge or drive; ICCU fuse state
note: ICCU (24V-204 and ODI PE23011 closing resume): three stated causes, over-current, overvoltage at end of HV charging, thermal loading during operation. Window set by the thermal-loading leg; rate by the transients. Evidence: heat-damaged FETs on warranty returns; replication attempted.

signals: crash-sensor pulse and ACU deployment decision recorded at the event (EDR)
note: Airbag control unit calibration deploys seat-mounted side airbags in frontal crashes with little lateral offset. The crash pulse and deployment record at the event identify it.

signals: cell-module voltage and self-discharge trend across parked periods and charge cycles; module temperature
note: HV cell modules may self-discharge (supplier deviations; shifted electrodes in recalled sub-populations) and go into thermal propagation; root cause stated as not clear. Vehicle data showed the self-discharge-detection software would have warned months ahead, so the stated mechanism (self-discharge) is observable as a long trend. Defective part is the cell module (out of scope); BMS software is the co-component.

signals: none (locates only: panel detachment at airbag deployment)
note: Insufficient vibration-weld adhesion of instrument-panel topper to airbag chute doors (supplier heat, power fluctuation, mat misalignment); part recreated by DOE.

signals: none (locates only: handling / ride-height anomaly)
note: Supplier mislabelled rear suspension modules; wrong module installed.

signals: none (locates only: disconnect fails to fire at a crash or battery event)
note: Non-functioning pyrotechnic battery disconnect shipped through a traceability gap on a new supplier line; found in a validation test. HV disconnect counted in scope (contactor / junction function).

signals: pack / contactor current during wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; contactor temperature and resistance history across sessions
note: BEC main-contactor design and part variation not robust to heat from multiple wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; accumulated heat damage and wear lead to arcing, failure to close or weld. The document states accumulation over multiple events, hence >700 s. Remedy is junction-box replacement; ODI RQ23004 resumes read.

signals: none (locates only: axle shift / clunk)
note: Torque tool falsely signalled final torque on transverse torque-rod fasteners; assembly error.

signals: 12 V rail voltage transients during the HLCM software upgrade; HLCM phase current and status (DTC)
note: 12 V voltage fluctuations during a software upgrade damage one of two HLCM (DC-DC) phases; converter capacity halves; later loss of propulsion. Taking the event as the phase damage, the 12 V transient seconds before identifies it. If the event were the later propulsion loss the span would be much longer; recorded as a boundary judgement.

signals: unclear (BMS diagnostic fault states)
note: BMS monitoring/diagnostic function may be impaired over time; FMVSS 305 warning might not activate. Description of cause NR; only a BMS software fault affecting diagnostics is stated, too thin to map a window.

signals: motor torque request and actual; wheel speeds (slip); vehicle speed; accel/decel sequence; drive-unit fault-monitor states; supply voltage
note: MCU/VCU torque-safety-monitor thresholds trigger a safe state (loss of motive power) in specific scenarios: low-speed wheel slip on ice, decel-to-accel at low speed, repeated back-to-back max accel/decel, false drive-unit fault monitors. Found in winter road testing. Sequences of seconds. MCU is in scope.

signals: none (locates only: seat non-latch warning)
note: Defective weld on second-row seat-frame latch; found in production-verification durability testing. Cause field NR; defect text states the weld defect.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: label content)
note: Sun visors carry non-US or no airbag warning labels (FMVSS 208 labelling); found in plant audit.

signals: none (locates only: cabinet detachment in a crash)
note: Cabinet bolts installed without required washers after a parts deviation; assembly human error.

signals: none (locates only: leveller alarm / fluid loss)
note: Leveling-jack hydraulic hoses not routed, secured or protected; chafing and heat blistering. Heat and chafe testing by engineering and an independent lab.

signals: none (locates only: tailgate-ajar state while moving)
note: Tailgate latch pawl perpendicular to catch; pawl walkout under dynamic loading (design weakness); analysis and testing.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: anchorage strength)
note: Second-row seat pedestal anchor brackets too weak for FMVSS 207/210; compliance test failure.

signals: cell-module voltage and self-discharge trend across charge cycles and parked periods; module temperature during and after charging
note: HV cell modules: two possible supplier causes (particle contamination, separator damage) leading to an internal short and overheating during or after charging. The remedy is self-discharge-detection software, so the internal-short mechanism is observable as a self-discharge trend; which of the two physical causes is not. Rated as PE070. Defective part is the cell module (out of scope).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: seat geometry)
note: Third-row bench seating width requires three designated seating positions but has two belts; regulatory interpretation error, confirmed by external testing institute.

signals: none (locates only: CAN loss / bus-off at the event)
note: Improperly retained DCFC loopback harness connector; CAN wire chafes on frame rail and shorts, temporary CAN loss, loss of propulsion. Defective part is wiring/harness retention.

signals: battery SOC and cell-voltage fluctuation across a full discharge cycle (drive to 20 % SOC); cell/pack temperature during quick charge
note: Excessive lithium deposits in battery cells raise resistance and cause SOC fluctuation; rapid heating in Level 3 quick charging. Remedy LBC/VCM software detects SOC fluctuation over a full monitoring cycle (documents state the cycle), hence >700 s. Description-of-cause field empty; mechanism stated in defect text. Defective part is the cells (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: gate swinging open)
note: Trailer inside gate has no secondary latch (design).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: guard strength)
note: Aluminium rear impact guard may not meet FMVSS 223 performance and labelling; cause stated as TBD (flagged), but any cause of guard strength is a structural property, so state 0 is mappable.

signals: none (locates only: string-open / fuse-blown warning, abnormal module voltage and temperature)
note: Same defect text as PE063 (Freudenberg module J-bar weld penetration; BMS software does not lock out the pack). Rated identically: stated cause is the weld, not signal-observable; out of scope (module internal busbar).

signals: SOC dwell at high state of charge across sessions; charging-current ripple from the charging infrastructure; cell voltages and temperatures
note: EQB HV battery cells (Farasis) may be insufficiently robust at high SOC: supplier early-production variation combined with external factors (charging-current ripple, mechanical damage); no specific root cause found. This campaign covers vehicles whose 25V-050 BMS update was not applied. The observable factors (high-SOC dwell, charging ripple) accumulate over sessions. Defective part is the cells (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: inflator rupture at deployment)
note: Curtain-airbag inflator lots with moisture introduced at supplier; internal corrosion and stress-corrosion cracking; field parts analysed.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: part variant)
note: Wrong-market steering wheel and driver airbag installed from an incorrect factory parts list (FMVSS 208).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: headrest design)
note: Third-row headrests not to specification (padding, catch groove); vehicle not reworked after validation tests; found in plant audit.

signals: none (locates only: fairing detachment)
note: Roof fairing adhesive bond: surfaces not properly prepped. Original report said cause under investigation; amended report states it.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: exit location)
note: Roof emergency exit in the wrong location for FMVSS 217 (regulation misread); design noncompliance.

signals: isolation-fault DTC and fault-severity class at the trip; HV shutdown state; gear state
note: Same defect as PE043 (non-school-bus population): vehicle control software misclassifies loss of isolation as a severe fault and shuts the HV system in motion. Rated as PE043.

signals: isolation-monitor DTC (single vs double isolation) and isolation-resistance values at the warning; HV shutdown state
note: Electric-drive-motor software cannot tell a single-isolation condition from a double-isolation condition in some production configurations and shuts the HV system 15-20 s after the warning. The fault classification and isolation readings at the warning identify it. Debris in the motor from supplier production is mentioned as a contributing possibility. A real isolation condition is involved, so not software-only.

signals: none (locates only: loose belt cable fastener)
note: Front seat-belt steel cable fatigues from repeated bending over the seat structure on entry (design weakness); returned-part analysis.

signals: ICCU / LDC voltage peaks and over-current transients; power-stage temperature history across charge and drive cycles; 12 V battery voltage
note: ICCU (24V-200; ODI PE23012 open and close resumes) damaged over time by transient high voltage and thermal cycling; returned ICCUs show damage after thermal cycling and voltage peaks. Rated as PE049.

signals: BECM SOH value versus pack age/odometer; displayed SOC versus cell voltages at the power limitation
note: Service-replacement BECM initialises SOH at 100 % instead of inheriting the pack SOH; SOC over-estimated, unexpected power limitation; lithium plating over many DC fast-charge cycles (second leg, which alone would need >700 s). For the power-loss event a snapshot (SOH 100 % on an aged pack, cell voltages at the limit) identifies it. Found from connected-vehicle data.

signals: none (locates only: belt slack in a crash)
note: End-fitting pretensioner locking impaired by gas blow-by at sealing piston (supplier manufacturing variation); found in conformity-of-production and sled tests.

signals: none (locates only: inflator rupture)
note: Roof-rail airbag inflator lot may have a manufacturing defect (end-cap separation / sidewall split); root cause still under investigation (flagged). Any inflator manufacturing cause is structural, so state 0 is mappable.

signals: none (locates only: arcing / loss of HV at the junction box)
note: Missing or loose bus-bar retention nuts in the HV battery junction box after a plant rework without torque re-verification (24V-144 scope amendment). Assembly error; in scope (junction box).
